newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton steady, no end to nine-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton steady, no end to nine-day strike.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Wednesday held steady in a narrow price band as a nine-day truckers strike continued to affect all commodities, dealers said.
Mill demand remained sluggish but limited supplies kept prices at previous levels.
"Transportation of cotton from the producing centres to the market and from market to the mills remained very low on account of the ongoing nationwide strike by transport operators," one broker said.
India's transport industry, on strike since April 1, is opposing the imposition of a service tax and a hike in insurance premiums.
"The export of cotton yarn and fabrics has been held up, in turn affecting demand for cotton by the mills and particularly spinning mills," he said.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi remained quiet at 915/960 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned was quoted at the previous level of 1,575/1,670 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) was quiet at 16,500/17,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) for the average variety and at the rate of 18,700/19,800 rupees per candy for the superior variety.
